key_findings.finding: The structure is highly polar and ionizable, with formula C18H18N8O7S3, MW 554.59, calculated LogP −1.61, TPSA 214.96 Å², HBD 4, HBA 13, and two Lipinski violations; these properties are consistent with poor passive membrane permeability and predominantly aqueous/ionic distribution rather than nonspecific lipophilic toxicity.
The available chemistry profile reports no valid PubChem record or GHS safety classification, so it does not directly establish a formal hazard label or clinical toxicity endpoint.

Given its approved clinical use, ceftriaxone would most likely be assigned the non-toxic/negative class in a ClinTox-style binary prediction of general clinical toxicity, while this should not be interpreted as absence of important adverse reactions; notable known risks include beta-lactam hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, biliary sludge or pseudolithiasis, rare immune hemolytic anemia, C. difficile-associated diarrhea, and rare neurotoxicity, with calcium–ceftriaxone precipitation risk in neonates.
